summary: Initramfs regression after SSD firmware flash prevents OS boot and blocks provisioning
description:
Issue summary: After applying an SSD firmware update in depot, devices fail to boot into the OS because initramfs generation does not include the newly required NVMe driver modules. This blocks automated reprovisioning and Intune device enrollment for affected units.

Impact: ~12 devices failed post-repair this week in staging depot; provisioning pipeline is failing with boot drops and the devices land in rescue shell. Blocked teams: Depot repair queue, imaging validation, and desktop provisioning.

Environment: Staging depot image (ubuntu-22.04-corp-image), kernel 5.15.0-204, nvme-fw v4.12.3 applied via vendor updater at depot. Affected hardware: Lenovo-ThinkPad-X1-Gen11, Dell-Precision-5570.

Observed behavior: After firmware flash and reboot, system drops to (initramfs) busybox, reporting: "modprobe: FATAL: Module nvme_core not found in directory /lib/modules/5.15.0-204-generic". initramfs prompt shows missing modules and fails to mount root (UUID mismatch reported). Intune agent never starts because OS doesn't reach systemd.

Expected behavior: Firmware flash should be compatible with existing kernel/initramfs packaging or imaging process should regenerate/initramfs with required modules so device boots and continues to Intune enrollment.

Additional context: Vendor firmware tool appears to rewrite NVMe controller ID which changes udev device ordering in a way that our dracut hooks don't detect. This may be a race between firmware tool and the initramfs building step in the depot post-flash workflow.
steps_to_reproduce: Start with fresh depot device imaged with ubuntu-22.04-corp-image (kernel 5.15.0-204).
Apply vendor NVMe firmware updater v4.12.3 (depot step), reboot as instructed.
Observe that on first reboot the system drops to (initramfs) busybox instead of continuing boot.
Inspect /lib/modules and run ls /lib/modules/5.15.0-204-generic to confirm missing nvme modules.
Attempt to chroot from live media and regenerate initramfs (update-initramfs -u) — in some cases the rebuild completes but subsequent boots still fail until a kernel package reinstallation is forced.
logs: (initramfs) modprobe: FATAL: Module nvme_core not found in directory /lib/modules/5.15.0-204-generic
udevadm settle timed out after 10s; device name change event observed: /dev/nvme0 -> /dev/nvme1
investigation_notes:
Initial hypothesis: firmware update changes controller identifiers leading to initramfs hooks not including new device symlinks. Collected images from two failed units; both show /etc/initramfs-tools/hooks/custom-nvme.sh missing or not executed in post-flash flow. Reproduction in staging confirmed when firmware tool is run before the 'regenerate-initramfs' step. Observed that vendor updater performs a cold reset causing udev to re-enumerate NVMe devices and our depot process does not wait for stable device paths.

We pulled the depot workflow logs: depot-agent step 7 (nvme-fw-flash) exits 0, immediately followed by step 8 (regenerate-initramfs). There is a 3-5s window where udev events still propagating. Adding a udevadm settle resolved one repro case locally.

Related code: boot-utils dracut hooks and imaging pipeline ordering (see linked PR).
comments: 2026-03-08 10:44 - Aisha Patel (depot-ops): Noticed two failed units this morning after routine NVMe firmware batch. Holding further firmware pushes until root cause confirmed.

2026-03-08 14:02 - SRE Oncall (Marta Rodriguez): Reproduced in staging, confirmed udev race. Temporary mitigation: insert 'udevadm settle' into depot post-flash step before update-initramfs. Will validate across models.
2026-03-09 09:15 - Imaging Eng (Noah Kim): Ran validation across 20 devices with inserted settle; 19/20 booted normally. One Dell still failed — investigating difference (older controller revision).

2026-03-10 16:30 - Vendor Support (WesternSSD): Opened case with vendor (case# WSSD-18293) to confirm whether firmware rewrite changes controller UUID mapping. Vendor acknowledged behavior on a subset of controllers and provided beta firmware that preserves mapping.
2026-03-10 18:05 - Marta Rodriguez: Mitigation deployed to staging: added udevadm settle + explicit update-initramfs -u step. Monitoring for 48h before rolling to prod depot.
resolution: Mitigation: Inserted 'udevadm settle' and explicit 'update-initramfs -u' into depot post-flash workflow. Short-term: paused vendor firmware batch for affected controller revisions. Long-term: vendor provided patched firmware; imaging team to add a pre-flash validation and post-flash validation step in CI. Follow-up task: INT-914579 to rollout updated workflow to prod after 48h stability window.
next_steps: Monitor affected staging queue for 48h after mitigation rollout.
Work with vendor to schedule controlled rollout of patched firmware to depot fleet.
Add automated imaging test case that runs NVMe firmware flash + reboot and checks for successful initramfs regeneration.
Create postmortem if >5% failure rate observed after firmware rollout.
